Subject: BYOK operator preflight simulation and key-eviction tabletop

Hi Morgan / Avalon IT Ops team and internal ops/security leads,

We want to run a short (90-minute) preflight tabletop exercise ahead of the planned BYOK cutover into Avalon Health's VPC private deployment. The goal is to validate:

- Operator access procedures to the on-prem HSM/KMS appliance
- Key rotation and emergency-eviction workflows (simulate operator loss and recovery)
- Secrets-handling constraints across the proxy layer and the operator agent
- Audit and evidence collection (log sampling we will need for your compliance team)

Attached is a lightweight preflight checklist and an initial tabletop scenario runbook. Please review and confirm who from Avalon will be the primary operator and the secondary (escrow) contact for the simulation. We will need:

1) A named on-call operator with console access (we will only simulate RM/eviction, no destructive ops).
2) Network window where we can briefly toggle the bastion route (5-10 minutes) without impacting production traffic.
3) Permission for the HSM vendor rep to join if we exercise vendor-assisted unseal.

Attachments: [attachment: byok-preflight-checklist.xlsx (xlsx)], [attachment: tabletop-scenario-notes.pdf (pdf)]

Proposed windows next week: Sep 22 10:00-11:30 PT or Sep 24 13:00-14:30 PT. Please confirm availability.

Thanks,

--

Great — Sep 24 works for Redwood ops. A couple of operational clarifications to make the simulation meaningful while keeping it safe: 

- We'll use a dedicated test keyset (k-test-*), scoped to the private deployment namespace. I will provision them on Redwood's staging HSM and export only the wrapped key material for the exercise.
- During the operator-eviction scenario we'll run three sub-tests: (A) operator credential revocation and immediate fallback, (B) threshold unseal with escrow holders, (C) key rotation and service rebind. Each sub-test will be <10 minutes.
- Request: Avalon to provide a short-lived service account with RBAC that we can elevate during the simulation (so we can validate role separation).
- We will not remove or change production ACLs; all changes will be limited to test namespace and test service identities.

Attached is the rotation matrix I mentioned. It lists required SSH bastion logs and the KMS audit events we will capture.

Attachments: [attachment: operator-credentials-rotation-matrix.csv (csv)]

Couple of compliance items to call out so the simulation maps to Avalon’s audit requirements: 

- Audit retention: ensure KMS/HSM operation logs for the test run are exported to Avalon-managed storage and retained per your policy (we'll tag them with HS-98327).
- Cryptographic policy: while this is a simulation, confirm we will exercise split custody on the test key (operator + Avalon escrow holder) and record the entire key ceremony flow in the audit trail.
- Evidence package: after the tabletop we will produce a short artifacts bundle: sequence of events, signed operator attestations, and the unseal transcript (sanitized). Please confirm whether Avalon prefers a PDF evidence package or a shared Drive folder with restricted access.

One caution: if we perform threshold unseal with vendor involvement, ensure the vendor's actions (account IDs) are visible in the audit logs. This is commonly requested by healthcare compliance teams.

I added scenario permutations to the tabletop notes (see attached) to exercise edge cases: partial network partition during rotation, delayed escrow response, and simulated operator credential compromise.

Hannah
Head of Security & Compliance
